Modern.brandNameRationale: Single word, technical term. Circular is the economic model the category is built around: products designed to return to the system, not the landfill. The brand sits on the principle directly. No flowers. No earth-photographs.
Modern.industrySummary: Sustainability brands keep using nature imagery. Trees. Leaves. The earth from space. The category has run out of room in that direction. The opening is for brands that look like product companies and lead with design and engineering, not imagery.
Modern.competitorLandscape: Patagonia (patagonia.com) is the institution. Vollebak (vollebak.com) does material-science-led modern. Pangaia (thepangaia.com) sits at the design-meets-science intersection. We sit closer to Vollebak in posture, with sharper brand work.
Modern.positioningStatement: Sustainable products engineered to come back to the system.
Modern.positioningRationale: Most sustainability brands lean on imagery and storytelling. We lead with the engineering: the materials, the take-back program, the next life of every product. The proof is in the system, not the photography.

targetAudience.primary: 30 to 50. Buys fewer, better things. Pays attention to materials. Returns the product when it's worn out. Reads the take-back program before buying.

dos: Name the material and the percentage
Show the take-back path
Skip the nature photography

Modern.logoDirection: A wordmark only. CIRCULAR in a tight modern grotesk, all caps, with the C set as a near-closed loop, almost a full circle. A standalone closed-loop circle icon for app, social, and on every take-back tag.

colorPalette.name: Loop Green
colorPalette.meaning: Cycle accent. The take-back tag color.

typography.primary: GT America for the wordmark and headlines
typography.secondary: GT America Mono for material specs and take-back data
typography.rationale: One family. The mono carries the technical material data and product lifecycle stats. The regular carries the brand.

customSections.body: No tree counting. No earth-from-space hero shots. No 'planet-friendly' copy. No carbon-offset partnerships used as marketing.

customSections.title: Where it lives
customSections.body: Every product ships with a take-back tag and a printed material lifecycle card. The website shows the percentage of returned products on the homepage. A printed annual report on what came back and what got remade.

Modern.brandDescription: Soil & Carbon is a modern sustainability consultancy specializing in regenerative agriculture, carbon accounting, and supply-chain transparency for food and consumer-goods companies.
Modern.scope:
Soil & Carbon works across:
• Regenerative agriculture transition consulting
• Carbon accounting and reporting (Scope 1, 2, 3)
• Supply-chain transparency and provenance tracking
• Annual sustainability report writing for client companies
• Published case studies of completed transitions
Modern.mission: To move food and consumer-goods companies from sustainability claims to sustainability operations.
Modern.vision: A consultancy whose published case studies are taught in supply-chain management programs.
coreValues: Direct — the engagement ends when the operations change.
Modern — sustainability as operations, not as marketing.
Operational — the deliverable is the change, not the recommendation.
Specific — every claim is documented and verifiable.
Modern.brandNameRationale: Soil names the foundational substrate of agriculture; Carbon names the foundational accounting unit of climate impact. Paired they reference both the source and the measurement of regenerative practice. Two-noun & paired naming follows the considered-modern sustainability school.
Modern.manifesto: Most sustainability consulting produces glossy reports. We started Soil & Carbon to produce operational change — regenerative agriculture transitions, carbon accounting that withstands audit, supply-chain transparency that customers can verify. The reports we write document what changed; we don't write reports that recommend change for someone else to do later.
Modern.industrySummary: Sustainability consulting has matured into a recognized category but most engagements end with a report, not with operational change. The opening is for a consultancy that takes engagements through to documented operational implementation.
Modern.competitorLandscape: South Pole (southpole.com) holds the closest peer slot in modern carbon-and-supply-chain consulting. ERM (erm.com) plays the heritage-environmental peer position. Anthesis Group (anthesisgroup.com) sits in the considered-modern peer middle. Climeworks Solutions (climeworks.com) plays the carbon-implementation peer reference. We belong alongside South Pole with a stronger regenerative-agriculture focus.
Modern.positioningStatement: Soil & Carbon is a sustainability consultancy specializing in regenerative agriculture transitions, carbon accounting, and supply-chain transparency.
Modern.positioningRationale: We compete on operational implementation rather than report production. Engagements end when the client operates differently, not when the report is delivered.

targetAudience.primary: Heads of sustainability, supply chain, and operations at food and consumer-goods companies of $100M-$5B revenue.
behaviors: Manage annual sustainability budgets and reporting cycles.
Sit through quarterly sustainability committee meetings.
Care about Scope 3 emissions, regenerative-agriculture transitions, and supplier audits.
Renew on multi-year engagement terms.
motivations: Need a consultancy that takes engagements through to operational implementation.
Need carbon accounting that withstands audit.
Need supply-chain transparency that customers can verify.

dos: Lead with the operational change rather than the framework.
Publish case studies with actual transition data.
Reference specific farms, suppliers, and audit firms by name where the client permits.
Sign engagement letters by the lead consultant.

messagingPillars.description: We design and implement on-farm transitions to regenerative practices for the client's supply chain, working directly with growers and suppliers.

messagingPillars.name: Carbon accounting that withstands audit
messagingPillars.description: Scope 1, 2, and 3 accounting documented to standards that third-party auditors accept. The accounting is the deliverable, not the report about the accounting.

messagingPillars.name: Supply-chain transparency
messagingPillars.description: Provenance tracking and supplier audit infrastructure that makes claims verifiable to customers.

typography.secondary: A clean grotesque for accounting tables and operational reports.
typography.rationale: The serif speaks. The grotesque measures.

Luxury.brandNameRationale: Two words from a different register. Garden and Estate belong to the older language of stewardship: the practice of caring for land across generations. The brand reframes sustainability as estate management, not activism.
Luxury.story: Garden & Estate began with a family that had spent four generations managing the same agricultural land. They wanted to share what they had learned with other owners of significant land. The firm advises on regenerative agriculture, woodland restoration, and long-term land stewardship.
Luxury.industrySummary: Sustainability at the top end has been chasing carbon credits and offsets. There's a parallel market for actual land stewardship, which is older, slower, and aimed at people who already own significant property. The customer is not buying sustainability. They are paying for someone to help them keep what they have.
Luxury.competitorLandscape: Pew Charitable Trusts (pewtrusts.org) operates at institutional scale. The Land Trust Alliance (landtrustalliance.org) handles the U.S. conservation easement side. Knepp Estate (knepp.co.uk) is the rewilding reference. We sit in their conversation, on the advisory side.
Luxury.positioningStatement: An advisory firm for landowners who want to keep their land well for the next century.

targetAudience.primary: Landowners of estates, ranches, working farms, and significant private holdings. Often inherited. Often working with one trusted family office. Looking for a firm that thinks in 50-year horizons.

dos: Address the client by surname
Speak in the language of land, not climate
Send paper reports each season

Luxury.logoDirection: A classical serif wordmark with elegant ligatures. A small hand-drawn ampersand becomes the firm's hallmark. A second mark, a single tree silhouette reduced to a trunk and three branch lines, used as the seal on every printed report.

colorPalette.name: Heritage Brass
colorPalette.meaning: Aged metal. The hardware on the estate gate.

typography.primary: Canela Text for the wordmark and printed material
typography.secondary: Söhne for the secure client portal
typography.rationale: A high contrast serif sets the heritage tone. A modern grotesk handles correspondence and digital surfaces. Both quiet.

Luxury.brandDescription: The Wickwood Foundation is a small private environmental research foundation operating across freshwater ecology, soil science, and forest restoration, funded by an endowment and a small group of patron families.
Luxury.scope:
The Wickwood Foundation works across:
• Freshwater-ecology research and field stations
• Soil-science research at long-term study sites
• Forest-restoration field experiments
• Annual scientific publications in peer-reviewed journals
• Patron-only annual research symposium
Luxury.mission: To support long-arc environmental research at a pace and quality commercial timelines usually prevent.
Luxury.vision: A foundation whose research is cited by the field for the next century.
coreValues: Senior — the foundation has supported research since 1971.
Discreet — research findings appear in journals, not press releases.
Considered — long-term study sites are the foundation's primary investment.
Patient — fifty-year data records are the standard.
Luxury.brandNameRationale: The Wickwood Foundation uses the definite-article + place-name + Foundation convention common to heritage environmental research foundations (The Nature Conservancy, The Wildlife Trusts, The Knepp Foundation tradition). Wickwood is a real but small English place-name with a wooded register. The Foundation suffix places the brand firmly in the small-private-research foundation tradition.
Luxury.manifesto: Most environmental work runs on grant cycles and corporate-CSR timelines. The Wickwood Foundation was endowed in 1971 to support environmental research on the long arc. We fund and operate long-term study sites in freshwater ecology, soil science, and forest restoration. The patron families have supported the foundation across generations.
Luxury.industrySummary: Premium environmental research is dominated by large universities and government bodies. There is a quieter market for the small private foundation operating long-term field stations and supporting long-arc research that university grant cycles cannot.
Luxury.competitorLandscape: The Nature Conservancy (nature.org) is the broad reference for environmental philanthropy. The Knepp Foundation (knepp.co.uk) holds the heritage rewilding peer slot. The Land Institute (landinstitute.org) sits in the long-arc agriculture-ecology peer position. The Bren School of Environmental Science & Management (bren.ucsb.edu) plays the academic environmental peer reference. We belong with The Land Institute and The Knepp Foundation in the small private-research foundation category.
Luxury.positioningStatement: A small private environmental research foundation operating long-term field stations in freshwater ecology, soil science, and forest restoration.
Luxury.positioningRationale: We do not pursue commercial projects. The foundation's mandate is basic environmental research. Funding comes from an endowment and a small group of patron families.

targetAudience.primary: Senior environmental scientists, patron families supporting environmental research, foundation programme officers, and academic collaborators.
behaviors: Publish in top-tier peer-reviewed journals.
Travel to field stations and research sites.
Care about long-term study site continuity.
Recommend visiting-scientist appointments to senior colleagues.
motivations: Want a research environment without commercial timelines.
Want long-term study sites with funding continuity.
Want a foundation that supports the long arc.

dos: Address correspondents by surname.
Sign correspondence by the foundation director.
Reference research publications by full citation.
Publish in established peer-reviewed journals only.
donts: No press releases on research findings.
No social-media presence beyond a single publications archive.

messagingPillars.name: Long-term field stations
messagingPillars.description: The foundation operates field stations at five long-term study sites, some with continuous data records of over fifty years.

messagingPillars.name: Endowment-funded
messagingPillars.description: The foundation is funded by an endowment established in 1971 and a small group of patron families who contribute annually. We do not pursue corporate funding.

messagingPillars.name: Patron-only symposium
messagingPillars.description: Once a year the foundation hosts a private research symposium for patrons, visiting scientists, and senior researchers. The symposium is the foundation's gathering.

colorPalette.meaning: Primary — the page colour of scientific publication.

colorPalette.meaning: Secondary — the colour of the foundation's namesake woodland.

typography.secondary: An old-style serif for body type in scientific papers.
typography.rationale: Letterpress register throughout. Publications use the foundation's heritage typography across decades.

Minimal.brandNameRationale: Single word. Says the entire philosophy of the brand in one syllable. Less is the actual sustainability practice, stripped of marketing. Less buying, less owning, less producing. The brand puts the principle in the brand position.
Minimal.industrySummary: Sustainability marketing has been about adding things. New brands, new materials, new labels. There is an opening for one that subtracts. One word. One promise. One product line that doesn't grow.
Minimal.competitorLandscape: Most sustainability brands compete on what they add. We compete on what we won't. The closest spirit is The Ordinary in skincare or Muji's discipline, applied to a sustainability-focused product line.
Minimal.positioningStatement: Sustainable goods. Fewer of them. Made to last.

targetAudience.primary: Adults who own less and want less. They don't want a new sustainability brand. They want the brand to stop launching things.

dos: Use plain words
Show what's in it
Tell customers when they don't need the product

Minimal.logoDirection: A wordmark only. LESS in a single weight grotesk, wide kerned, all caps. No icon. The product line is a small number of items that never gets larger. The wordmark appears on each. That's the system.

typography.rationale: One face. One purpose. Nothing decorative.

Minimal.tagline: A small waste-services company. One service.
Minimal.brandDescription: Compost is a minimal residential composting service operating in a defined service area, with a single service tier and a published fixed monthly fee.
Minimal.scope:
Compost works across:
• Weekly residential food-waste pickup within a defined service area
• Single fixed monthly subscription fee
• Return of finished compost to subscribers twice a year
• Plain published service-area map
• Annual single-page company report
Minimal.mission: To operate one good residential composting service indefinitely.
Minimal.vision: A composting service whose 100th week of operation is identical in form to its first.
coreValues: Plain — one service, one fee.
Direct — the map is the marketing.
Considered — the service does one thing well.
Minimal.brandNameRationale: Compost is the real waste-services trade word for the product of decomposed organic matter — single trade word, deeply specific to the category. Single-word naming follows the modern minimal services school (Tend, Wisp, Carton register).
Minimal.manifesto: Most waste-services companies expand into multiple service categories — composting, recycling, junk removal, hauling. We made Compost because the actual best small waste service does one thing well. Residential composting pickup. One service. One fee. One service area.
Minimal.industrySummary: Residential composting services have grown in metropolitan areas but most expand into adjacent waste services. There is real space for a minimal service that strips the offering to weekly residential composting and refuses to add adjacent categories.
Minimal.competitorLandscape: CompostNow (compostnow.org) plays the closest peer in residential composting subscription. Hometown Habitat (hometownhabitat.com) holds the considered-local peer slot. Soiltech (soiltech.com) sits in the regional composting peer position. We sit further out — one service, one fee, one defined service area.
Minimal.positioningStatement: Compost is a residential composting service offering weekly food-waste pickup at a single fixed monthly fee within a defined service area.
Minimal.positioningRationale: We strip the service offering. One service. One fee. One service area. No expansion into adjacent waste categories.

Subscribe to weekly residential services.

motivations: Want a simple weekly composting pickup.

The opening is a structured, mid-size advisory firm focused on enterprise.

Corporate.brandDescription: Greenholt Environmental Holdings operates a portfolio of environmental services brands across waste management, soil remediation, water treatment, and ecological restoration categories.
Corporate.scope:
Greenholt Environmental Holdings works across:
• Multi-brand environmental services operations
• Shared regulatory compliance across jurisdictions
• Industrial and municipal contracts

Corporate.mission: To provide a serious operating platform for mid-tier environmental services brands that want to keep their identity and outsource the operations.
Corporate.vision: An environmental services operator whose portfolio brands grow under their own names because the regulatory and capital infrastructure are shared.
coreValues: Senior — partners deal with partners.
Operational — regulatory compliance runs on schedule.
Reliable — capital-equipment capacity supports brand operations.
Discreet — brand and client relationships stay private.
Corporate.brandNameRationale: Greenholt is a constructed compound place-name (green + holt, where holt is the archaic English word for a small wood or grove) with a heritage holding-company register. Environmental Holdings follows the multi-brand operator naming convention used in environmental services (Veolia, Waste Management, Republic Services structure). The pair reads as an institutional operator with multi-brand portfolio scale.
Corporate.manifesto: Greenholt Environmental Holdings owns and operates a portfolio of environmental services brands. Each brand retains its identity, technical leadership, and customer relationships; we operate the shared regulatory compliance, capital equipment, and back office. The buyer is a brand founder considering sale, a municipal procurement officer, an industrial client seeking consolidated supplier relationships, or an institutional investor holding environmental-services assets.
Corporate.industrySummary: Environmental services has consolidated under a small number of large multi-brand operators (Veolia, Waste Management, Republic Services, Clean Harbors). The opening underneath is for a regional mid-tier multi-brand operator with deep compliance operations and the procurement-grade reliability municipal and industrial clients require.
Corporate.competitorLandscape: Veolia (veolia.com) is the multi-service environmental reference at scale. Republic Services (republicservices.com) holds the multi-category peer slot. Clean Harbors (cleanharbors.com) sits in the multi-service environmental peer position. Casella Waste Systems (casella.com) plays the regional peer reference. We belong in the regional mid-tier multi-brand environmental-services operator category.
Corporate.positioningStatement: Greenholt Environmental Holdings is a regional multi-brand environmental services operator running waste management, soil remediation, water treatment, and ecological restoration across a portfolio of brands.
Corporate.positioningRationale: We compete on shared regulatory compliance, capital-equipment depth, and the procurement-grade reliability municipal and industrial clients require for multi-year operating relationships.

Creative.tagline: A sustainability brand for the boring practical work.
Creative.brandNameRationale: Common Ground references both shared earth and shared political space. Project frames the work as ongoing. The naming follows the considered-creative environmental brand school.
Creative.manifesto: Most sustainability brands are too earnest to take seriously. They moralize. They scold. They make you feel bad. We made Nice Planet because climate work should be possible without becoming a different person. We're serious about the work. We're not serious about ourselves.
Creative.industrySummary: Sustainability branding has been earnest, beige, and slightly preachy. There's room for one that's loud, warm, full of personality, and still serious about the actual work. The category has been quiet for too long.
Creative.competitorLandscape: Allbirds (allbirds.com) does sustainability with restraint. Patagonia (patagonia.com) does it with conviction. Climate Town (the YouTube channel) does it with humor. We are closer to Climate Town in tone, applied to a brand and product company.
Creative.positioningStatement: A sustainability brand for people who want to do something without feeling guilty about the rest of their life.

Creative.brandDescription: The Mending Co is a creative-led sustainability brand operating a repair service for clothing, household goods, and small electronics, with a service-by-mail model and a published repair philosophy.
Creative.scope:
The Mending Co works across:
• Repair services for clothing, household goods, and small electronics
• Service-by-mail with prepaid return shipping
• Published repair-or-not assessments before work begins
• Quarterly published essays on the repair tradition
• Annual repair-club gatherings in three cities
Creative.mission: To make repair a normal household choice rather than a virtuous exception.
Creative.vision: A repair service whose mailroom queue is full of household objects on their second, third, and fourth life.
coreValues: Warm — repair is care for the things we own.
Specific — every assessment is written for the item.
Considered — some assessments recommend not repairing.
Literary — the writing about repair is part of the brand.
Creative.brandNameRationale: The Mending Co names the foundational repair practice — mending is the archaic verb for repairing clothing and small textile goods. The definite article + Co suffix follows the considered-creative trade-name school. Stands in the lineage of declarative repair brands (Patagonia Worn Wear's spirit, iFixit's craft register, The Restory's repair tradition).
Creative.manifesto: Most household objects are designed to be replaced, not repaired. We started The Mending Co to make repair a normal household choice. Send us the garment, the lamp, the leather bag, the small appliance. We assess it. We give you an honest repair-or-not recommendation. If we repair it, we send it back with a printed repair record.
Creative.industrySummary: Repair services exist but are fragmented across cobblers, tailors, electronic repair shops, and small craft repair operations. There is real space for a creative-led brand that operates a multi-category repair service by mail with a clear philosophy and consistent quality.
Creative.competitorLandscape: Patagonia Worn Wear (patagonia.com/worn-wear) plays the closest peer in considered repair operations. The Restory (the-restory.com) holds the leather-and-luxury repair peer slot. iFixit (ifixit.com) sits in the electronics repair-tooling peer position. Rejean (rejeansjeans.com) plays the denim-repair peer reference. We sit alongside Patagonia Worn Wear with a multi-category by-mail model.
Creative.positioningStatement: The Mending Co is a multi-category repair service operating by mail, with a published repair philosophy and an honest repair-or-not assessment before any work begins.
Creative.positioningRationale: The brand competes on the repair philosophy and on the honest assessment. Every item gets a written assessment before work begins; some assessments recommend not repairing the item.

targetAudience.primary: Households 30-55 with possessions they'd rather repair than replace — leather goods, well-made clothing, small electronics, household appliances.
behaviors: Own items they've kept for years and would like to keep longer.
Care about repair as a household practice.
Send items for repair when local options aren't available.
Want honest assessments about repair feasibility.
motivations: Want a repair service that handles multiple categories.
Want an honest assessment before paying for repair.
Want a brand that argues for repair as normal household practice.

dos: Publish the repair philosophy and assessment process.
Photograph repaired items before, during, and after.
Sign assessments by the lead repair specialist.
Reference completed repairs by item type and age in case studies.

messagingPillars.name: Multi-category repair
messagingPillars.description: We repair clothing, household goods (lamps, vases, small furniture), leather (bags, shoes, belts), and small electronics. The categories are the menu.

messagingPillars.name: Honest assessment
messagingPillars.description: Every item begins with a written assessment — what the repair would entail, what it would cost, whether it's worth doing. Some assessments recommend not repairing.

messagingPillars.name: Quarterly essay
messagingPillars.description: Once a quarter the brand publishes an essay on the repair tradition — history, craft, philosophy. The essay is the brand's primary marketing artefact.

Creative.logoDirection: A wordmark — The Mending Co set in a quiet display serif with a small illustration of a needle-and-thread beside it. The mark reads as printed on a heritage tailor's receipt.

colorPalette.name: Linen
colorPalette.meaning: Primary — the page colour of the repair record.

colorPalette.name: Thread
colorPalette.meaning: Secondary — the colour of mending thread.

colorPalette.name: Wax
colorPalette.meaning: Single accent — the colour of the brand's signature wax seal.

typography.primary: A quiet display serif for the wordmark and the quarterly essay.
typography.secondary: A book serif for repair records and assessments.
typography.rationale: Two related serifs. The brand reads like a heritage tailor's notebook.
